doc.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021

title: First night at Small's and seeing Omer Avital
summary: Her first visit to Small's in New York, seeing Omer Avital play, and an all-night hang before the bus back to Boston.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: In your bio there’s a brief anecdote about you finally arriving in New York and going to Small’s. And I wonder if that, I can only envision if maybe that was a moment to remember for you — what was that like to sort of step into a club and say okay, this is a big part of the New York scene and how do I fit into this.

Wow that’s a beautiful question because you really brought me back to that moment. I mean the name of the club is called Small’s, which still exists, so I didn’t know what it was. I didn’t know at that time when I stepped into Small’s it was a new club that was encouraging young people to find who they are through the tradition of bebop and hard bop, but open the doors for experiments for people to write their own music and to make their own bands, and I just witnessed a couple of people that I knew, because there was a bass player that I knew since I was in high school, used to play with my older brother Yuval, his name is Omer Avital and Omer was a key figure at the time at Small’s. And I

walked into Small’s and he’s — there he was just playing the bass, swinging his butt off, and being part of the scene. And so for me more than thinking of like what is Small’s or the scenes of New York, for me it was kind of the idea that somebody from Israel, from a different country, from where I come from, from my city, can just be part of a whole new culture and mingle so well and excel. So there was a few other Israelis at the time that were part of that scene, so for me it was, and I remember that night I mean we definitely pulled an all-nighter that trip because we were students, we had no money, we were there at Small’s and we had to spend — Small’s was open the whole night after the shows. There was like a show at 10 PM, at midnight, at 2 AM, then a jam session all night and then of course at 6 AM we took the bus back to Boston where I was still a student at Berklee. So we had to stay there, no matter what, so we were just kind of like watching all these amazing — the hang. The hang basically.
